findings.description: The MySQL 8.0 parameter group does not set require_secure_transport = 1 (nor any TLS-related parameter), so the catalog database will accept unencrypted client connections, allowing credentials and data in transit to be observed on the network.

The instance user_data embeds the RDS master username and the password variable (var.password) in cleartext, writing them to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is retrievable by anyone who can reach the instance metadata service (including via SSRF from the PHP app) and is visible in the AWS console/API and Terraform state.

No metadata_options block is specified, so IMDSv1 (token-optional) remains enabled. Combined with an attached instance profile (catalog_app_profile) and a web application, a server-side request forgery can be used to steal the role's temporary credentials and the plaintext DB credentials in user data.

No root_block_device/ebs_block_device with encrypted = true is configured, so the instance's EBS volumes may be created unencrypted, leaving the database credential file written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc stored at rest without encryption.

The bootstrap installs and starts httpd serving the data-entry application over plain HTTP with no TLS configuration or redirect, so form submissions (employee names/addresses) and any session data traverse the network in cleartext.

The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the database storage, and its snapshots, are unencrypted. Catalog data and credentials stored on disk are exposed if the underlying storage or a snapshot is accessed.

publicly_accessible = true assigns the MySQL instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, dramatically expanding the attack surface of a data store that should only be reachable from within the VPC.

The master password is taken from var.password and the master username is hard-coded to the predictable value 'admin'. A plaintext Terraform variable password is persisted in state and, combined with a default admin username and a public endpoint, enables credential guessing/brute force against the database.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role assumed by the internet-facing catalog_app_server EC2 instance. Compromise of that instance yields full control of all S3 data, EC2 infrastructure and RDS instances in the account, including a privilege-escalation path (e.g. modifying DB master credentials or launching instances with other roles).

The database security group allows all protocols and ports outbound to 0.0.0.0/0, which permits data exfiltration and command-and-control callbacks from a compromised database host rather than restricting egress to required destinations.

No parameter forcing TLS (e.g. require_secure_transport) is applied at the instance level and the instance is publicly reachable, so MySQL connections may be negotiated in cleartext over untrusted networks.
